key_insight: UPEBNL makes causal Bayesian network learning scalable for EHR-based cancer prescreening while keeping the model structure interpretable.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help clinicians and researchers understand which patient factors and evidence pathways contribute to esophageal and colorectal cancer risk predictions.
method: Adaptive data slicing to split large EHR datasets for parallel learning
Quality-aware structure aggregation to combine local network results
Global DAG construction to produce a stable causal-interpretable network
evidence_signal: In simulations it improved structural recovery by nearly 40% and sped up conventional CBN learning by up to 221.28-fold; in EHR prescreening it reached AUCs of 0.8171 for esophageal cancer and 0.784 for colorectal cancer.
watch_item: The learned network is based on observational EHR data, so causal direction and generalizability still need careful external validation before real-world use.
paper_title: Scalable Causal-Interpretable Machine Learning for Cancer Prescreening Using Electronic Health Records
